notes: Educational sports passages. Rules can vary by competition and format; consult the applicable current regulations for official decisions.

passages.title: Why Teamwork Matters
passages.body: A team may have talented individuals, but talent alone does not guarantee success. Players need to communicate, understand their roles, and support one another. In football, a defender may pass to a midfielder instead of attempting a difficult solo run. In basketball, a player may pass to a teammate in a better position. Teamwork helps a group use its strengths together.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of teamwork?
options: It allows every player to ignore their role
It helps players combine their strengths
It guarantees that the team never loses
It removes the need to communicate
questions.explanation: Teamwork combines individual abilities through communication, roles, and support.

passages.title: Understanding Offside in Football
passages.body: The offside rule is designed to prevent attackers from gaining an unfair advantage by waiting close to the opponents’ goal. In general, at the moment a teammate plays the ball, an attacking player is in an offside position if they are nearer to the opponents’ goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent. Being in an offside position alone is not automatically an offence; involvement in active play matters.

questions.question: When is an attacking player’s position judged for offside?
options: When the ball reaches the goal
At the moment a teammate plays or touches the ball
When the referee blows the final whistle
When the goalkeeper catches the ball
questions.explanation: Offside position is assessed at the moment the teammate plays or touches the ball, with involvement in active play also required.
references: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 11

passages.title: What Run Rate Means in Cricket
passages.body: A cricket team’s run rate is the average number of runs scored per over. If a team scores 60 runs in 10 overs, its run rate is 6 runs per over. Run rate helps describe scoring speed, but it does not show the full match situation by itself. Wickets remaining, overs left, pitch conditions, and the target can all affect a team’s strategy.

questions.question: A team scores 72 runs in 12 overs. What is its run rate?
options: 5 runs per over
6 runs per over
7 runs per over
8 runs per over
questions.explanation: Run rate is total runs divided by overs: 72 ÷ 12 = 6.

passages.title: The Basketball Shot Clock
passages.body: In basketball, the shot clock limits how long a team may control the ball before attempting a shot that reaches the basket under the rules. In major FIBA competitions, the shot-clock period is 24 seconds. This rule encourages attacking play and prevents a team from holding the ball for too long without trying to score.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the shot clock?
options: To give players a rest period
To encourage teams to attempt a shot within a time limit
To decide which player is captain
To measure the total length of the match
questions.explanation: The shot clock limits possession time before a qualifying shot attempt.
references: FIBA Official Basketball Rules, shot-clock provisions

passages.title: Why Athletes Warm Up
passages.body: A warm-up prepares the body and mind for physical activity. It may include light movement followed by movements related to the sport. A football player might jog and practise controlled changes of direction before intense drills. A warm-up should be appropriate to the athlete and activity; it is not a guarantee against injury, but it can help athletes prepare to perform.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a warm-up?
options: To exhaust the athlete before training
To prepare the body and mind for activity
To replace all training
To guarantee that injuries cannot happen
questions.explanation: A warm-up prepares an athlete for the demands of the activity but cannot guarantee injury prevention.

passages.title: The Purpose of a Cool-Down
passages.body: After intense exercise, an athlete may gradually reduce activity by walking or doing gentle movements. This transition is called a cool-down. It gives the body time to move from hard effort toward rest. A cool-down should not be confused with a guarantee that soreness will disappear; recovery also depends on training load, sleep, nutrition, and other factors.

questions.question: What does a cool-down help an athlete do?
options: Move gradually from intense activity toward rest
Immediately increase maximum speed
Replace sleep and nutrition
Guarantee no muscle soreness
questions.explanation: A cool-down provides a gradual transition from exercise to rest.

passages.title: Cricket Powerplay
passages.body: In limited-overs cricket, powerplay overs have fielding restrictions that influence attacking and defensive decisions. Batters may look for scoring opportunities because fewer fielders are allowed outside the inner circle, while bowlers and captains plan how to limit runs. The exact restrictions depend on the format and playing conditions.

questions.question: Why can powerplay overs affect batting strategy?
options: Because the ball becomes larger
Because fielding restrictions can create scoring opportunities
Because no bowler is allowed to bowl
Because the innings automatically ends
questions.explanation: Fielding restrictions can create gaps and change risk-reward decisions for batters.

passages.title: Tennis Scoring
passages.body: Tennis uses a distinctive scoring sequence within a game: love, 15, 30, 40, and game. If both players reach 40, the score is called deuce. Under the standard advantage system, a player must win two consecutive points from deuce to win the game: first gaining advantage, then winning the next point.

questions.question: What must a player generally do to win a game from deuce under the advantage system?
options: Win one point only
Win two consecutive points
Win the next set immediately
Change sides of the court
questions.explanation: From deuce, a player needs advantage and then the following point.
references: International Tennis Federation Rules of Tennis

passages.title: Passing the Baton in a Relay
passages.body: In a relay race, each runner completes part of the team’s distance and passes a baton to the next runner within the designated exchange zone. A smooth exchange requires timing, communication, and practice. A team can lose valuable time through a slow handover or be disqualified if the exchange does not follow the rules.

questions.question: What is essential for a legal and efficient relay exchange?
options: Passing the baton anywhere on the track
Timing the handover within the exchange zone
Throwing the baton to the next runner
Stopping the race during each exchange
questions.explanation: Relay baton exchanges must follow the event's exchange-zone rules and require coordination.
references: World Athletics Competition and Technical Rules

passages.title: Pacing in a Marathon
passages.body: A marathon is a long-distance race of 42.195 kilometres. Runners often plan a pace they can sustain instead of starting at maximum speed. Beginning too fast can make the later stages much harder. A sensible pacing strategy considers preparation, conditions, experience, and the runner’s own limits.

questions.question: Why is controlled pacing important in a marathon?
options: It helps conserve effort for the full distance
It guarantees a world record
It means the runner never needs training
It makes the course shorter
questions.explanation: A sustainable pace helps runners manage effort over a long distance.
references: World Athletics, marathon distance and endurance-racing principles

passages.title: A Penalty Kick in Football
passages.body: A penalty kick is awarded for certain direct-free-kick offences committed by a defending player inside their own penalty area while the ball is in play, subject to the Laws of the Game. The kick is taken from the penalty mark. The goalkeeper must follow positioning rules, and other players must remain outside the penalty area and penalty arc until the kick is taken.

questions.question: Where is a football penalty kick taken from?
options: The centre circle
The penalty mark
The corner arc
The halfway line
questions.explanation: A penalty kick is taken from the penalty mark.
references: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 14

passages.title: What Is a No-Ball in Cricket?
passages.body: A no-ball is an illegal delivery under cricket’s playing laws and conditions. Reasons can include certain types of overstepping or dangerous and unfair deliveries. The batting side receives an extra run in many common formats, and the delivery does not count as one of the over’s legal balls. The exact consequences can vary with the type of no-ball and competition rules.

questions.question: What is generally true about a no-ball?
options: It is always counted as a legal ball
It is an illegal delivery and usually gives the batting side an extra run
It automatically ends the innings
It means the batter is out
questions.explanation: A no-ball is an illegal delivery; common consequences include an extra run and the ball not counting in the over.
references: MCC Laws of Cricket; relevant competition playing conditions

passages.title: The Goalkeeper’s Role
passages.body: A football goalkeeper protects the goal, organises the defence, and may help start attacks by distributing the ball. The goalkeeper has special privileges to handle the ball within their own penalty area, subject to the Laws of the Game. Good goalkeeping involves positioning, communication, decision-making, and safe technique.

questions.question: Which task is part of a goalkeeper’s role?
options: Using hands anywhere on the field
Protecting the goal and organising defenders
Taking every throw-in
Ignoring the defensive line
questions.explanation: Goalkeepers defend the goal and communicate with teammates; handling privileges are limited by the rules.
references: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 12

passages.title: Rebounding in Basketball
passages.body: A rebound occurs when a player gains possession of the ball after a missed field-goal or free-throw attempt, subject to the rules. An offensive rebound gives the attacking team another chance to score, while a defensive rebound helps the defending team end the opponent’s possession. Positioning and timing are important for both.

questions.question: What does a defensive rebound usually help a team do?
options: Give the opponent another immediate shot
Gain possession and end the opponent’s attack
Add three points automatically
Restart the game from the centre circle
questions.explanation: A defensive rebound gives the defending team possession after a missed shot.

passages.title: Sportsmanship in Competition
passages.body: Sportsmanship means competing honestly, respecting opponents and officials, and accepting results without abusive behaviour. A player can be disappointed after losing, but should not insult the other team or deliberately break the rules. Respectful conduct helps make sport fairer and more welcoming for everyone involved.

questions.question: Which action demonstrates good sportsmanship?
options: Arguing with officials through insults
Congratulating opponents and respecting the result
Cheating when the referee cannot see
Mocking a teammate after a mistake
questions.explanation: Respect, honesty, and fair conduct are central to sportsmanship.
references: Olympic values and general fair-play principles

passages.title: Hydration During Sport
passages.body: The body loses water through sweat and breathing, especially during prolonged exercise or hot conditions. Athletes should plan fluid intake according to the activity, environment, and individual needs. Drinking excessively can also be harmful, so more is not always better. Athletes should follow qualified guidance for demanding events and pay attention to their own circumstances.

questions.question: Which statement about hydration is most accurate?
options: Every athlete should drink exactly the same amount
Fluid needs can vary with activity and conditions
Water is never needed during exercise
Drinking as much as possible is always safest
questions.explanation: Hydration needs vary; excessive fluid intake can also be dangerous.

passages.title: Strength Training for Athletes
passages.body: Strength training can help athletes develop the ability to produce force and control movement. Exercises may use body weight, resistance bands, or weights. Good programmes match the athlete’s age, experience, sport, and goals. Correct technique and gradual progression are more important than lifting the heaviest possible load.

questions.question: What should guide an athlete’s strength-training programme?
options: Using the heaviest weight every session
Age, experience, sport, goals, and sound technique
Copying every exercise seen online
Ignoring recovery
questions.explanation: Appropriate programming and technique matter more than simply lifting maximum weight.

passages.title: Why Recovery Matters
passages.body: Training places demands on the body. Recovery allows athletes to adapt and prepare for future sessions. Sleep, appropriate nutrition, rest days, and sensible training loads all contribute. Training harder every day without recovery can reduce performance and increase the risk of overuse problems. A good programme balances effort with recovery.

questions.question: Why should athletes include recovery in a training plan?
options: Because improvement happens only during competition
Because recovery supports adaptation and readiness for future training
Because rest removes the need for practice
Because every athlete needs the same rest schedule
questions.explanation: Recovery is part of training adaptation and helps manage fatigue.

passages.title: The Corner Kick
passages.body: A corner kick is awarded when the whole ball passes over the goal line, on the ground or in the air, last touched by a defending player, and a goal is not scored. The attacking team takes the kick from the corner area nearest to where the ball left the field. Teams may use planned movement to create space for a shot.

questions.question: When is a corner kick generally awarded?
options: When the attacking team last touches the ball over the goal line
When the defending team last touches the ball over its own goal line and no goal is scored
Whenever a player falls
After every goal
questions.explanation: A corner is awarded when the defending team last touches the ball before it crosses its own goal line without a goal being scored.
references: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 17

passages.title: What Does Taking a Wicket Mean?
passages.body: In cricket, a wicket can refer to the dismissal of a batter, the set of stumps and bails, or the pitch depending on context. When a team takes a wicket, it has dismissed a batter. Wickets are important because a batting side has a limited number of dismissals available, and losing them can change its scoring strategy.

questions.question: In the phrase “the bowling team took a wicket,” what does wicket mean?
options: The batter was dismissed
The innings gained ten runs
The ball became dead for the whole match
The umpire changed ends
questions.explanation: In this match context, taking a wicket means dismissing a batter.

passages.title: The Three-Point Line
passages.body: In basketball, a successful field goal scored from beyond the three-point line is worth three points. The player’s position is judged according to the rules at the time of the shot. A team may use long-range shooting to stretch the defence, but a three-point attempt can be more difficult than a closer shot.

questions.question: How many points is a successful shot from beyond the three-point line worth?
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.explanation: A successful field goal from beyond the three-point line counts for three points.

passages.title: Different Swimming Strokes
passages.body: Competitive swimming includes several recognised strokes, such as freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly. Each has different body positions, arm movements, and kicking patterns. Learning correct technique helps swimmers move efficiently and follow event rules. Freestyle events generally allow the swimmer to use any style, although front crawl is commonly used because of its speed.

questions.question: Which stroke is commonly used in freestyle races?
options: Butterfly only
Front crawl
Breaststroke only
Backstroke only
questions.explanation: Freestyle permits any style, and front crawl is commonly chosen for speed.

passages.title: The Long Jump
passages.body: In the long jump, an athlete runs along a runway and takes off from a board or take-off area to land in a sandpit. The measured distance is based on the nearest mark in the landing area made by any part of the body, measured back to the take-off line according to the rules. Speed, take-off technique, and body control all matter.

questions.question: What is the athlete trying to maximise in the long jump?
options: Time spent in the air only
The legal measured distance of the jump
The height of the runway
The number of steps after landing
questions.explanation: The goal is to achieve the greatest legal measured distance.

passages.title: The High Jump
passages.body: In the high jump, an athlete attempts to clear a horizontal bar without dislodging it. The athlete chooses an approach and take-off technique, then lands on a safety mat. Competitors usually progress through increasing heights, and the event uses rules for failed attempts and tie-breaking. The Fosbury Flop is a well-known technique in which the athlete goes over the bar back-first.

questions.question: What is the main objective in the high jump?
options: To clear the bar at the greatest possible height
To jump the longest distance horizontally
To run the fastest lap
To throw an object the farthest
questions.explanation: High jump athletes aim to clear the highest height without dislodging the bar.

passages.title: Shot Put Basics
passages.body: Shot put is a field event in which an athlete puts, or pushes, a heavy metal ball called a shot from the shoulder. It is not thrown like a baseball. The athlete must stay within the circle and follow the event’s landing-sector and exit rules. Technique, strength, balance, and timing all contribute to distance.

questions.question: How is the shot supposed to be released?
options: Pushed from the shoulder
Kicked from the ground
Thrown like a baseball overarm
Rolled along the runway
questions.explanation: The shot is put from the shoulder rather than thrown like a ball.

passages.title: Drafting in Cycling
passages.body: When cyclists ride closely behind another rider, the leading rider blocks some air resistance for the rider behind. This effect is called drafting. It can help the following cyclist save energy, especially at higher speeds. Riders still need to maintain control and leave enough space to respond safely to sudden changes.

questions.question: Why does a cyclist draft behind another rider?
options: To increase air resistance
To reduce the effort needed to overcome air resistance
To make the bicycle heavier
To avoid pedalling
questions.explanation: Riding in another cyclist’s slipstream can reduce aerodynamic drag.

passages.title: Rotation in Volleyball
passages.body: In indoor volleyball, a team rotates positions in a clockwise direction when it wins the right to serve from the opponent. Rotation helps players take turns in different court positions. Players must follow the correct order at the moment of service, although they can move into tactical positions after the ball is served.

questions.question: When does a volleyball team rotate?
options: After every point, regardless of which team served
When it wins the right to serve from the opponent
Only at the end of a set
Whenever the coach asks
questions.explanation: The receiving team rotates when it wins the right to serve.

passages.title: Three Hits in Volleyball
passages.body: A team generally has up to three hits to return the ball over the net, not counting a block contact under the rules. Players often use a pass, a set, and an attack. The sequence requires communication because teammates must avoid letting the ball fall or making an illegal fourth team hit.

questions.question: What is the usual maximum number of team hits to return the ball, excluding a block contact?
options: One
Two
Three
Five
questions.explanation: The team generally has three hits, with block contact treated separately under the rules.

passages.title: A Badminton Rally
passages.body: Badminton is played with a shuttlecock, which players hit over a net. A rally continues until the shuttle lands on the court, goes out, fails to cross the net, or a fault occurs. Players use clears, drops, smashes, and net shots to move an opponent and create openings. Accuracy and recovery to a good court position are important.

questions.question: What ends a badminton rally?
options: A player changing their grip
The shuttle landing, going out, or a fault occurring
A player moving to the back of the court
The audience cheering
questions.explanation: A rally ends when the shuttle is no longer legally in play, such as landing or a fault.
references: Badminton World Federation Laws of Badminton

passages.title: Spin in Table Tennis
passages.body: Players can brush the ball at different angles to create topspin, backspin, or sidespin. Spin changes how the ball travels and how it bounces, making it harder for an opponent to return. Reading the racket angle and the ball’s movement helps a player choose an appropriate response.

questions.question: Why is spin useful in table tennis?
options: It changes the ball’s movement and bounce
It makes the table larger
It allows a player to catch the ball
It removes the need for footwork
questions.explanation: Spin affects flight and bounce, creating challenges for the opponent.

passages.title: Weight Classes in Boxing
passages.body: Boxing competitions use weight classes so that opponents compete within defined weight limits. This helps make matchups more balanced, although weight is not the only factor affecting performance. Skill, experience, conditioning, and strategy also matter. Athletes must follow the event’s weigh-in rules rather than attempting unsafe last-minute weight changes.

questions.question: Why are weight classes used in boxing?
options: To guarantee identical skill levels
To create more balanced matchups based partly on body weight
To decide who is the referee
To remove the need for rules
questions.explanation: Weight classes help organise fairer matchups by limiting differences in competitor weight.

passages.title: Scoring in Wrestling
passages.body: Wrestling rewards actions such as takedowns, exposure, and controlled positions according to the style and competition rules. A takedown generally involves bringing an opponent to the mat while gaining control. The details of scoring differ between freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling, so athletes must learn the rules of their event.

questions.question: What is a takedown in wrestling generally intended to achieve?
options: Bring the opponent to the mat while gaining control
Send the opponent out of the building
Stop the match permanently
Score by kicking the opponent
questions.explanation: A takedown involves bringing the opponent down and establishing control under the relevant rules.

passages.title: The Chess Clock
passages.body: In timed chess, a chess clock gives each player a limited amount of time to make their moves. After making a move, a player presses their side of the clock, starting the opponent’s time. Managing the clock is part of competitive strategy: a player must balance careful thinking with the need to make moves before time expires.

questions.question: Why is a chess clock used?
options: To measure the size of the board
To limit and manage each player's thinking time
To decide which pieces are strongest
To replace the rules of chess
questions.explanation: The clock controls each player's allotted time in a timed game.

passages.title: The Role of Officials
passages.body: Referees and umpires apply the rules of a sport and make decisions during competition. Their role is to support fair play and manage the match. Officials may make difficult decisions under pressure, and systems such as video review are used in some sports and competitions. Players should raise concerns through the proper process rather than intimidation.

questions.question: What is the main role of a match official?
options: Support one team regardless of the rules
Apply the rules and manage the competition
Choose the winner before the match
Replace the players
questions.explanation: Officials apply the rules and help manage fair competition.

passages.title: Leadership by a Team Captain
passages.body: A captain can help a team stay organised, communicate with officials when appropriate, and encourage teammates. Good leadership is not simply giving orders. It includes listening, staying composed, accepting responsibility, and setting an example through effort and respect. A captain should support the team’s shared plan rather than seek personal attention.

questions.question: Which behaviour shows effective team leadership?
options: Blaming teammates publicly
Listening, communicating, and setting a positive example
Ignoring the coach and teammates
Taking credit for every success
questions.explanation: Effective leadership combines communication, responsibility, and example.

passages.title: Creating Space in Team Sports
passages.body: In games such as football and basketball, players can create space by moving away from defenders, making runs, and passing at the right time. A player without the ball can still help the team by drawing a defender away or opening a passing lane. Good tactics involve understanding where teammates and opponents are positioned.

questions.question: How can a player without the ball help create space?
options: Stand still in a crowded area
Move intelligently to draw a defender or open a passing lane
Ignore the play
Block a teammate's movement
questions.explanation: Off-ball movement can create options and space for teammates.

passages.title: Communication in Defence
passages.body: Defenders need to communicate about opponents, space, and possible threats. A clear call such as “man on” or “switch” can alert a teammate to pressure or a change in marking responsibility. Silence can cause two defenders to leave the same space uncovered. Communication should be brief, early, and understood by the team.

questions.question: Why is clear defensive communication important?
options: It helps teammates respond to threats together
It guarantees that opponents cannot score
It replaces physical positioning
It is useful only after the match
questions.explanation: Timely communication helps a defensive unit coordinate its actions.

passages.title: The Importance of Fielding in Cricket
passages.body: Fielding is more than stopping boundaries. Fielders can save runs, catch batters out, prevent overthrows, and create pressure through quick and accurate returns. A strong fielding side supports its bowlers by limiting easy scoring opportunities. Concentration matters because one missed chance can change the match.

questions.question: How does good fielding support a cricket team?
options: It only makes the match look faster
It can save runs and create dismissal opportunities
It replaces the need for bowlers
It automatically adds runs to the batting side
questions.explanation: Fielding can prevent runs and create chances to dismiss batters.
references: MCC Laws of Cricket; general cricket tactics

passages.title: A Declaration in Test Cricket
passages.body: In Test cricket, a captain may declare an innings closed even when the team could continue batting. A declaration is a tactical decision intended to give the team enough time to dismiss the opposition and pursue a result. It involves balancing the size of the lead, time remaining, pitch conditions, and match situation.

questions.question: Why might a captain declare an innings in Test cricket?
options: To give the opposition more runs automatically
To leave enough time to try to dismiss the opposition
Because the innings has reached exactly ten overs
To cancel the match
questions.explanation: A declaration can create time for a team to bowl the opposition out and seek a result.

passages.title: Football Formations
passages.body: A football formation describes how outfield players are arranged across defensive, midfield, and attacking lines. A 4-3-3 formation, for example, usually describes four defenders, three midfielders, and three forwards. Formations can change during a match as players move and coaches adjust tactics. The numbers do not describe the goalkeeper.

questions.question: What does the 4-3-3 formation usually represent?
options: Four goalkeepers, three referees, three substitutes
Four defenders, three midfielders, three forwards
Four forwards, three defenders, three goalkeepers
The number of goals expected
questions.explanation: The formation numbers describe the usual distribution of outfield players by line.

passages.title: The Counterattack
passages.body: A counterattack happens when a team quickly moves from defending to attacking after winning possession. It can be effective when the opposing team has committed many players forward and left space behind. A successful counterattack needs quick decisions, accurate passing, and support from teammates. Speed alone is not enough if the team loses control of the ball.

questions.question: When can a counterattack be especially effective?
options: When the opponent has left space while attacking
When all teammates stand still
When the team refuses to move forward
When passing is deliberately inaccurate
questions.explanation: A counterattack can exploit space left by opponents who have moved forward.

passages.title: What Endurance Means
passages.body: Endurance is the ability to sustain physical activity over time. It matters in distance running, cycling, swimming, and many team sports. Athletes develop endurance through appropriately planned training, with gradual increases and recovery. Endurance is different from maximum strength, although sports can require both qualities.

questions.question: Which athlete relies strongly on endurance?
options: A marathon runner maintaining effort over a long distance
A weightlifter performing one maximum lift only
A sprinter reacting at the start only
A shooter holding a static position only
questions.explanation: A marathon runner must sustain physical effort over an extended period.

passages.title: Agility in Sport
passages.body: Agility is the ability to change direction or body position quickly while maintaining control, often in response to a changing situation. It is useful in sports such as football, basketball, badminton, and tennis. Agility involves more than running fast in a straight line; it includes balance, coordination, and decision-making.

questions.question: Which example best demonstrates agility?
options: Running a straight 100-metre sprint only
Changing direction quickly to respond to an opponent
Holding a weight without moving
Standing still for a long period
questions.explanation: Agility involves controlled changes of direction or movement in response to demands.

passages.title: Reaction Time
passages.body: Reaction time is the time between noticing a signal and beginning a response. A sprinter reacts to the starting signal, while a goalkeeper responds to a shot. Good performance may depend on anticipation as well as reaction speed. Athletes practise recognising cues so they can prepare their movements earlier.

questions.question: What is reaction time?
options: The total length of a match
The time between a signal and the start of a response
The number of points scored
The time needed to recover after sleep
questions.explanation: Reaction time measures how quickly a person begins responding after a stimulus.

passages.title: Flexibility and Movement
passages.body: Flexibility refers to the range of movement available at a joint or group of joints. It can help athletes perform sport-specific movements comfortably and with control. Flexibility needs differ between sports and individuals. Training should be appropriate and should not force painful ranges of motion.

questions.question: What does flexibility describe?
options: The ability to move a joint through a range of motion
The number of goals scored
The speed of a ball
The weight of sports equipment
questions.explanation: Flexibility concerns the available range of movement at joints.

passages.title: The Principle of Specificity
passages.body: The principle of specificity means training should relate to the demands of the sport or performance goal. A swimmer benefits from swimming practice, while a football player needs work on skills and movement patterns used in football. General fitness can support performance, but sport-specific practice helps develop the relevant abilities.

questions.question: What does training specificity mean?
options: Every athlete should do exactly the same training
Training should relate to the demands of the target sport or goal
Training should avoid practising sport skills
Only strength training matters
questions.explanation: Specific training develops abilities relevant to the activity being prepared for.

passages.title: Progressive Overload
passages.body: Progressive overload means gradually increasing training demands as the body adapts. This may involve adding a small amount of resistance, distance, repetitions, or complexity over time. Increasing too much too quickly can create excessive fatigue and raise injury risk. Progress should be planned and adjusted to the athlete’s response.

questions.question: What is a sensible example of progressive overload?
options: Doubling every training load overnight
Gradually increasing training demand as adaptation allows
Never changing training difficulty
Training through serious pain
questions.explanation: Progressive overload is gradual and should be matched to recovery and adaptation.

passages.title: Why Athletes Use Training Plans
passages.body: A training plan organises sessions around goals, competition dates, skill development, and recovery. It helps athletes avoid random workloads and track what they have done. Plans should be reviewed when performance, health, or circumstances change. A plan is a guide that supports decisions, not a reason to ignore warning signs.

questions.question: What is a useful purpose of a training plan?
options: To organise training and recovery around clear goals
To guarantee victory
To prevent all changes in schedule
To make every session equally difficult
questions.explanation: A plan helps organise training load, goals, and recovery while remaining adjustable.

passages.title: Fair Play
passages.body: Fair play means following the rules and respecting the spirit of competition. A player should not deliberately deceive officials or harm an opponent to gain an advantage. Fair play also includes respecting teammates, opponents, and spectators. Winning matters in sport, but the manner of competing matters too.

questions.question: Which action is against fair play?
options: Following the rules
Respecting the opponent
Deliberately trying to injure an opponent
Accepting an official decision respectfully
questions.explanation: Deliberately harming an opponent violates the spirit of fair competition.
references: Olympic values and general fair-play principles

passages.title: Making Sport Inclusive
passages.body: Inclusive sport aims to give people with different abilities and backgrounds meaningful opportunities to participate. Adaptations may include modified equipment, accessible facilities, or adjusted formats while preserving the purpose of the activity. Inclusion is not simply allowing someone to attend; it means considering what enables them to take part safely and with dignity.

questions.question: What is an example of making sport more inclusive?
options: Refusing all adaptations
Providing accessible facilities and suitable equipment
Assuming everyone has identical needs
Excluding beginners from practice
questions.explanation: Inclusion involves practical adaptations that support meaningful participation.
